messages:
Priya K: paging — dedicated-reserved pool for eu-west-1 hit 100% and queue depth spiked. Multiple enterprise tenants affected, including AcmeCorp reserved reservation. Autoscaler kept failing to add nodes. Incident bot: pager triggered.
alerts-bot: Alert: dedicated-resv-pool-eu-west1_utilization >= 0.99 for 3m — Severity: P1
Devin (oncall): I’m on it, grabbing logs and current allocations. @Jin @Tara please standby.
Michael S: I see steady enqueue at 12k req/min, token churn high, lots of mid-size chat sessions. KV cache hit rate dropped.
Jin (infra): checking GPUs — all NGC-rt instances show 100% mem and ~95% util. No obvious OOM.
Tara (platform): Autoscaler errors in the controller: `scale_request_rate_limited` repeated. Looks like we hit cloud provider API rate limits when trying to provision more GPU nodes.
Devin (oncall): Copy. Can we fall back to reserved spare capacity / burst pool?
Priya K: Customer SLA first — shift AcmeCorp workloads to fallback cluster in us-west-2 if possible. Elena, can you notify AcmeCorp SRE that we’re seeing degraded perf?
Elena (Customer Success): Notifying now, message: "We’ve detected capacity saturation in eu-west-1 impacting your reserved workloads. We are actively migrating traffic and will provide ETA shortly."
Michael S: Quick mitigation steps I'm running: 1) scale down low-priority tenants in eu-west-1, 2) apply temporary throttles to non-enterprise routes, 3) attempt manual node create with higher rate quotas.
Devin (oncall): Execute step 1 and 2 — use `resvctl evict --policy=noisy-tenant --threshold=80%` to target noisy reservations.
Jin (infra): Running eviction command now. Output:
```
$ resvctl evict --policy=noisy-tenant --threshold=80%
Eviction plan generated: tenants [spike-play, test-queue-42] marked for preemptive eviction
Applied: 2 reservations drained, informing scheduler
```
Devin (oncall): Preempted two noisy tenants, reclaiming 2 GPUs. Queue depth down 18% — helpful but not enough.
Tara (platform): Manual scale attempt to create 3 nodes returned 429s: `RateLimitExceeded: Too many create requests`. Cloud tickets open.
Michael S: Alternative: cold-migrate AcmeCorp sessions to a dedicated fallback variant (smaller model) to reduce token throughput while preserving service. Can we switch model variant for their reservation?
Priya K: Yes — start canary: route 10% of AcmeCorp sessions to gpt-lite-3 (quantized) hosted on existing infra. That should reduce per-token GPU time by ~40%.
Devin (oncall): Implemented routing override: `route override --tenant=acmecorp --percent=10 --model=gpt-lite-3` — applied. Monitoring.
alerts-bot: Metric update: queue_depth(eu-west-1) 1420 -> 1123 after evictions and routing change (5m). Latency for AcmeCorp 95th went from 1.9s -> 1.4s for the canary.
Elena (Customer Success): AcmeCorp acknowledged; they asked for ETA and if we can guarantee no token loss. I told them we’re migrating live sessions and will avoid interruption.
Priya K: Good. Next: we need to reduce autoscaler pressure so we don't keep hammering cloud API. Jin, can you increase controller backoff/retry and batch create requests?
Jin (infra): Pushing a hotfix to the scaler: increase `create_batch_size` to 5 and backoff to 10s. Patching now.
sre-bot: Deploy started: scaler-hotfix v1.2.3 -> canary on controller-2
Devin (oncall): While that rolls, we should also enable short-term token-based admission control to shed non-critical requests at the gateway. Tara, can you flip the throttle rule?
Tara (platform): Flipped `gateway.admission.control` to `reservations_only` for 10m windows for lower tiers. Rule: reject new low-priority sessions with 429 and retry-after header.
Michael S: Observability: adding a quick eval on output quality for AcmeCorp on gpt-lite-3 to ensure no regression. If quality drops, rollback canary.
Elena (Customer Success): Customer noted temporary 10% routing looks acceptable. Asking for proactive report when fully migrated.
Devin (oncall): Autoscaler patch rolled to primary — successful, and subsequent node create calls now succeed (no 429). Creating 4 nodes now.
Jin (infra): Node create log snippet:
```
2026-03-15T02:14:12Z SCALE: creating 4 gpu-nodes batch_size=4
2026-03-15T02:14:47Z SCALE: nodes provisioning ok - 4/4
```
Priya K: Nice work. Add nodes freed up more capacity; queue depth at 5-min averaged 600.
Michael S: Post-mitigation, AcmeCorp 95th latency back to 1.0s. No error rate increase.
Devin (oncall): Action items for post-incident: 1) Pager root cause — autoscaler hitting provider rate limit + noisy tenant causing sustained saturation, 2) Short-term: eviction policy + routing to quantized model + manual scale, 3) Long-term: increase reserved burst capacity for enterprise reservations and implement provider rate-limit-aware backoff in scaler, 4) Run noisy-tenant detection runbook to refine thresholds.
Priya K: Agree. Also add: automated fallback routing for enterprise reservations when local pool reaches 85% for >3m.
Tara (platform): I’ll own the fallback routing feature and the regression test matrix for quantized variants.
Jin (infra): I’ll file a ticket with cloud provider to raise create rate quota and attach logs.
Michael S: I'll draft a short customer-facing postmortem blurb for AcmeCorp and coordinate with Elena.
Elena (Customer Success): Sending: "Follow-up: we migrated 100% of impacted sessions to fallback nodes, provisioning completed within 18m, latency restored. Will provide formal RCA later."
Devin (oncall): All good to close page once metrics stable for 30m. Setting follow-up timer.
alerts-bot: Reminder set: check metrics at +30m
Priya K: Thanks team. Quick retro note: consider an on-call playbook step to try routing to quantized variants before eviction for better customer experience.
Michael S: Noted. Adding to postmortem.
Devin (oncall): Closing thread summary: root cause = mixed (noisy tenant + provider rate limit). Mitigations executed = eviction, temporary throttles, canary routing to quantized model, manual scale and autoscaler patch. Customer impact = performance degradation for AcmeCorp for ~18m, no data loss. Next steps = implement fallback routing, raise provider quotas, refine noisy-tenant detection, update runbook.
Priya K: tagging for postmortem: @Tara @Jin @Michael @Elena @Devin.
Elena (Customer Success): Will coordinate customer follow-up and schedule a sync with AcmeCorp tomorrow PST.
Devin (oncall): End of thread — leaving notes in incidents tracker and creating a postmortem draft."
